name: espresso mule
instructions:
First drink recipe in this cookbook. Two ingredients: ginger ale + a shot of espresso, combined carefully.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- ginger ale (I use a sugar-free sparkling water version — ginger/lime flavored sparkling water; see notes)
- 1 shot of espresso

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Pour ginger ale into a glass.
2. SLOWLY combine the shot of espresso with the ginger ale — the temperature differential between hot espresso and cold carbonated ginger ale will cause an explosion of foam if you dump it in fast. Pour the espresso in gradually, or pour it down the side of the glass, to keep the foam under control.
3. Serve.
notes:
=== SLOW COMBINE — TEMPERATURE DIFFERENTIAL CAUSES FOAM EXPLOSION ===

The critical technique note: hot espresso + cold carbonated ginger ale = massive foam eruption if combined too fast. The heat destabilizes the CO2 all at once. Combine SLOWLY — either drizzle the espresso in a thin stream or pour it down the side of the tilted glass so it slides in gradually. Rushing this step gets you a foam eruption over the glass rim.

=== I USE SUGAR-FREE SPARKLING WATER GINGER ALE (GINGER/LIME FLAVORED SPARKLING WATER) ===

My version uses a sugar-free sparkling water product — flavored ginger/lime sparkling water — rather than a traditional sugared ginger ale. Cleaner, less sweet, and the ginger + lime + espresso combination reads more like a proper adult mule than the syrupy result you'd get from Canada Dry / Schweppes. If you want the traditional sugared-ginger-ale version, that works too, but it'll read sweeter and closer to a soda-fountain drink than a mule.
